MEASURED ON REFLOW2'S OWN ORIENTATION CALL, 2026-08-16, and it is this epoch's own theme firing on the instrument a new session reads FIRST. `loop_status` reported '1 answered question(s) never reached the design — write the answer in, or acknowledge the gap'. The answer HAD reached the design: `dec:the-authority-check-guards-forward-not-backward` is accepted, dated 2026-08-11, carries an AUTHORED_BY role=approver edge to who:ajs and a GOVERNED_BY edge from the rule it shapes, and records the ruling, both rejected options and the measurement behind them. The claim was false and I repeated it to the user as fact before checking.

THE CODE CANNOT SUPPORT WHAT THE MESSAGE ASSERTS. report.rs:755 is `questions.iter().filter(|q| q.status == "answered").count()`. That knows one thing — the question is answered and its gap is still open — and the message turns it into a claim about whether design nodes exist. Nothing looks for them.

AND THE STATE IT FLAGS IS DELIBERATE, which is what makes this `req:a-deliberate-state-is-not-a-defect` rather than a wording bug. The decision says in its own text that it does NOT close the gap: the gap is `unverified_enforced_rule`, it needs a PASSING Verification, none exists, and closing it would record a judgement the owner did not make. So the correct action — rule, record it, leave the debt honestly open — is exactly what makes the instrument report false debt, and the only ways to silence it are to acknowledge a gap that is real or to stop recording rulings.

THE FIX IS NOT OBVIOUS AND IS NOT ASSERTED HERE: 'was this answer written into the design' has no general computation, since an answer may land as a Decision, a Requirement, a status move or an edge. The narrow honest repair is for the message to say what it actually knows.
